summary:
Observed 2026-10-23 during SC2 reserved-storage rehearsal r3 (#4746; #4516 comments 6363630329, 6363830442, 6363866613, 6363978038). Host-root `os.mkdir('fsgg-sc2-reserved', 0o711, dir_fd=<guest /var/tmp>)` failed with `OSError: [Errno 75] Value too large for defined data type` (EOVERFLOW).

Cause (kernel rule): the source comment names `may_o_create()` in fs/namei.c, which is the `open(O_CREAT)` path; `mkdir` goes through the equivalent creation check in the same file (`may_create_dentry()`, `may_create()` in older kernels), checked against upstream source in this PR's review. Both return -EOVERFLOW when the caller's fsuid/fsgid has no mapping in the target filesystem's user namespace (`fsuidgid_has_mapping`). A rootless Podman container's rootfs (overlay) is mounted inside the container's user namespace (here `uid_map 0 100000 65536`), and host uid 0 is not mapped there. So no host-root-owned object can ever be created in a rootless guest's tree, including the fdev container's `/var/tmp`. The design point `parent is host-root 0711` was infeasible; production would have failed identically. The same defect applied to the binder's per-operation leaf, which was created by host root with a `uid == 0` check one step after the parent. Removal is different: the delivery comment states that the uninstall's guest-leaf `rmdir` through nsenter as host root stays permitted, because it creates nothing and needs only CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE over inodes whose ids are mapped in the init namespace (asserted by the author and not challenged in review; rehearsal r4 then ran its guest-leaf `rmdir` with rc 0, #4516 comment 6363978038, accepted in 6363985779).

Rule (option A, decided and delivered as C1 r1d plus the binder): create the object as the guest's root. Read `uid_map`/`gid_map` relative to a held `/proc/<pid>` fd; require exactly one row with inside id 0, count >= 1 and outer id != 0; take that outer id (here 100000:100000). In a forked child holding the directory fd, call `setfsgid` then `setfsuid` (libc), confirm each by a second call returning the new value (else refuse), `mkdirat(dir_fd, name, mode)`, open the directory and `fchmod(mode)` (this beats the umask), `os._exit`, and return errno over a pipe so EEXIST stays `FileExistsError`. The caller's credentials never change, and any child crash, signal or failure refuses. Owner checks change from `uid == 0` to `uid == outer(guest 0)` (parent 0711, leaf 0700); host root and the unprivileged developer owner are refused. Alternatives considered: B, a target outside the overlay (needs a container recreate, not available for the live container); C, `podman exec --user root mkdir` (equal ownership, but outside the fd chain).

Trust note: only the guest's root can rename or replace objects so created, which is the engine owner's `podman exec --user root`, the same boundary the identity-proof helper already accepts; the unprivileged guest user cannot write the 0711 parent. The accepted closure of #4746 also records that the guest `developer` account has in-container sudo, so that protection against agents inside the guest is cooperative, not adversarial: an agent could deny service but not escape the container boundary. Review accepted the residual that `fchmod` reopens by name, so guest root could swap the leaf in between; the identity and mount-id pins catch it. Binder pins fix the parent identity and mount id at bind time, and a parent swap after the bind does not move the mount.

Limits: observed with Podman rootless on one host, a single-range uid_map and a kernel of the Home host; unit tests cannot prove the real root-in-userns path, which rests on rehearsal r4 (#4516 comment 6363978038) and the production install reported in the #4746 closure. A different uid_map shape (multiple rows, or inside 0 unmapped) is refused, not handled. Evidence scripts and hashes stay in Home custody. The cited document supplies only the generic diagnostic-execution failure-custody expectation. No operation is authorized by this record.
title: Host root cannot create objects in a rootless container's tree (EOVERFLOW); create as the guest's mapped root via setfsuid in a forked child
